sts_ep1_12_final_scene: choice 221 option 0 "Fine, finish your op." leads (character attitude/mortality nodes 272 -> 1556 -> 313 -> ...) to exit "End peace", the only route that feeds the milko_alive writer in sts_ep1_12_phase.

sts_ep1_01_final section 345: anderson "Gaspar's dead." / nika "What?! You're lying!"; it feeds the fact writer 524 and then choice 243 ("You killed him for parts?" / "Least he didn't suffer." / "Brother did it to himself.").

rules.statement: In Treating Symptoms, V agreed to let Alan Noël finish his NetWatch operation and left Milko Alexis alive instead of carrying out the hit.
V closed the Treating Symptoms gig without killing Milko Alexis; Hands' debrief said his NetWatch contacts put the client, Indira Barazza, under round-the-clock netrunner protection instead.

After Treating Symptoms, Alan Noël messaged V that the NetWatch operation had paid off: Milko led them to the man behind the Voodoo Boys' old Militech bots, a Belgrade arms dealer selling them to separatists.
Hands closed V's Dogtown Saints gig as premium work: the scavengers were dealt with and Anthony Anderson came out of it alive.
The Haven clinic confrontation in Dogtown Saints ended with Anthony Anderson killed by Nika; Hands' debrief acknowledged Anderson's death while noting the scavengers had been cleared out.
In Prototype in the Scraper, V talked Hands into having a chrome-doc recover the Zetatech implant from Hasan Demir and letting Hasan go free instead of handing him back to Zetatech; Hands agreed.
In Heaviest of Hearts, V had the forged testimony against Michael Maldonado deleted outright; Hands reported that Maldonado had nothing but praise for V.
V's Heaviest of Hearts job turned into a fight inside Heavy Hearts, Hands' own club; his debrief chided V for making such a mess there.
In Roads to Redemption, V got into the stadium weapons factory and uploaded Nele's software to the Crimson Harvest Net-nuke, disarming it before it could be used.
At the end of Spy in the Jungle, V handed Mark Bana's biomonitor over to the agents for Ana Friedman to use, rather than suppressing it as Steven Santos had asked.
After Spy in the Jungle, Hands noted that Mark Bana's fate was all over the news once the biomonitor reached the agents, and that what mattered to him was that they had been paid.
V ended Spy in the Jungle by leaving Mark Bana's biomonitor at Hands' drop point, as Steven Santos had urged, instead of giving it to Ana; Hands approved of V's "good sense".
V followed Steven Santos' request and left Mark Bana's biomonitor at the fixer's drop point instead of giving it to Ana; Steven later reached out to V, grateful for V's part in it.
When V met Ana Friedman and Steven Santos at the end of Spy in the Jungle, V destroyed Mark Bana's biomonitor in front of them instead of handing it over.
Some time after V got him out of Dodger's den, Bill Mitchell messaged V that he had laid down his badge to open a business of his own in the Glen.
V took Fiona Vargas' controlled leak instead of her full client data; Hands passed it to the client but complained the roster was shorter than expected and lacked heavier hitters.
V refused Fiona Vargas' offer and took her full client data; Hands' debrief said the Europeans could now make sure the tax evaders were punished.
During the BD shoot V directed, V convinced Tool he was Lina Malina's long-lost sister; the TooLina scroll worked, and Lina later messaged V that it was exactly what her brand needed.
V texted Hands that the "kidnapped Lina Malina" gig was really about Edgar Tool, who believed he was Lina, and that V had convinced him he was her sister.
During the BD shoot V directed, V convinced Tool that he was a clone created by the FIA. It was a script for the shoot, not a fact about Tool.
V texted Hands that the client was really Tool, a BD-rental owner who believed he was Lina Malina, and that after V freed him he now thought he was an FIA clone.
During the BD shoot V directed, V handed Tool his own fan letter as his lines; it brought Edgar Tool back to himself, ruining the scroll Lina Malina had expected to film.
V texted Hands that the client had been stuck believing he was someone else after a BD accident, and that V had helped him back to his old self.
V texted Hands that the "Lina Malina" client was really Tool, a BD-rental owner locked in the basement by his business partner, and that V had simply set him free.
To get Lina Malina to the BD shoot, V transferred her the advance she demanded by text and sent her the Brainporium address.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that, by some miracle, Jago and Bennett were working in tandem and Dogtown had never been this well run.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that Jago was dead and gone and that Bennett now ran Dogtown on his own.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that Bennett was no longer missed and that Jago was running Dogtown better than expected.
After Run This Town, Hands messaged V that Jago, Dogtown's new top dog, had stopped by his office for tea to discuss business.
In Shot by Both Sides, V sided with Bree Whitney: the objective to kill Dante was completed, and Hands then told V the client was pleased and paid.
Hands warned V by holocall that Bree Whitney had sold Militech's data to NetWatch and vanished, and that NetWatch had dispatched a hunter in the aftermath.
Once V had finished every job Hands had in Dogtown, he invited V to Heavy Hearts for a reward and a proper goodbye, and V met him there to collect it.
As promised for Yoko's help, V texted Mr. Hands the coordinates of Reed's convoy ambush site, the road by the abandoned hotel on Pacifica Blvd.
